candidates.summary: TestSplitURLKeepsTrailingSlash is 10 lines that catch no mutation the other tests miss; deleting it is 10 lines to 0 with no coverage lost
candidates.failure_scenario: A maintainer changing splitURL reads two tests covering the trailing slash and keeps both in step. Deleting the dedicated one and trimming the slash inside splitURL turns TestSplitURL, TestCanonicalURL, TestCrawlerInScope, TestURLToFile and TestURLToFileIsSafe red, so the 10-line test only costs a reader the question of what it adds. Its measurement (62,174 vs 48,642 bytes) is the part worth keeping: move that comment onto TestSplitURL's own "/r/x/y/" row, which already pins the exact base.
candidates.verify_by: delete func TestSplitURLKeepsTrailingSlash, run `go test ./...` in misc/gnopreview (green), then add `p = strings.TrimSuffix(p, "/")` to splitURL and run again (five tests red)
candidates.evidence: With the function deleted: `ok github.com/gnolang/gno/misc/gnopreview 0.004s`. With it deleted and splitURL trimming the slash: `--- FAIL: TestSplitURL ... splitURL("/r/x/y/") = "/r/x/y","",""; want "/r/x/y/","",""`, plus FAIL on TestCanonicalURL, TestCrawlerInScope, TestURLToFile and TestURLToFileIsSafe.

candidates.summary: TestSeedsSkipSingleSegmentDirs asserts only absence, so it stays green on a Seeds() that emits no directory page at all; one reflect.DeepEqual is 10 lines to 5 and pins both sides
candidates.failure_scenario: Seeds() walks up to the directory pages with `strings.Count(d, "/") >= 2`. Change that bound to >= 3 and Seeds() returns no directory page for any realm, so the crawl seeds only the realm's own three pages and every /r/<namespace> listing falls through to the live site. The whole package still passes, this test included: it looks for "/r" and "/p" and finds neither, which is also true when nothing was seeded. The deeper form is one equality against the four seeds the function actually returns, which rejects both the over-seed the test names and the under-seed it cannot see.
candidates.verify_by: in misc/gnopreview change crawl.go's `strings.Count(d, "/") >= 2` to `>= 3` and run `go test ./...`: expect red, observe ok; then replace the loop with `reflect.DeepEqual(c.Seeds(), []string{"/r/gnoland/home", "/r/gnoland/home$source", "/r/gnoland/home$help", "/r/gnoland"})` and repeat
candidates.evidence: Unmutated: `Seeds() = []string{"/r/gnoland/home", "/r/gnoland/home$source", "/r/gnoland/home$help", "/r/gnoland"}`. With >= 3: `Seeds() = []string{"/r/gnoland/home", "/r/gnoland/home$source", "/r/gnoland/home$help"}` and `ok github.com/gnolang/gno/misc/gnopreview 0.005s`. TestB9SeedsAssertionIsOneSided in the artifact reproduces it without touching crawl.go.

candidates.summary: the `maxSlugLen+16` bound is 7 chars looser than anything slug() can emit (73), so the assertion passes on a digest half again as wide; `maxSlugLen+9` is the exact bound and the same one line
candidates.failure_scenario: slug() truncates to maxSlugLen and appends "-" plus 8 hex chars, so its longest segment is 73. The test allows 80. Widen the digest from sha256[:4] to sha256[:6] and segments reach 77: TestURLToFile and TestMapURL go red on their hardcoded digests, and TestURLToFileIsSafe, the test whose whole subject is that a long argument produces no unbounded segment, stays green. The +16 is a fudge with no derivation beside it; the bound the code can actually produce is maxSlugLen+9.
candidates.verify_by: in misc/gnopreview replace both `hex.EncodeToString(sum[:4])` in crawl.go with `sum[:6]` and run `go test -run TestURLToFileIsSafe ./...`: expect red, observe ok; then set the bound to maxSlugLen+9 and repeat
candidates.evidence: Probe on the head tree: `seg len 73 (maxSlugLen=64, bound used by the test=80)`. Under the sha256[:6] mutation the failures are `--- FAIL: TestMapURL` and `--- FAIL: TestURLToFile` only — TestURLToFileIsSafe does not appear.

candidates.summary: TestWantFile never calls wantFile: it drives inScope and chargeFile, so its green depends on three early returns the function it is named for does not own
candidates.failure_scenario: wantFile (crawl.go:227) is the changed-set-vs-budget decision. The test named for it asserts through inScope, which returns false before ever reaching wantFile on RenderOnly, on a path carrying both render args and a tab query, and on a trailing slash. Add a fourth early return to inScope and this test still passes while the decision it claims to cover is no longer exercised for those paths; a maintainer grepping wantFile finds a test that proves something else. Either call c.wantFile(realm, name) directly, or name the test for inScope's file gate, which is what it measures.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'wantFile' misc/gnopreview/*.go: the only call site is inScope at crawl.go:209, and crawl_test.go's TestWantFile body calls c.inScope and c.chargeFile and never c.wantFile
candidates.evidence: grep over misc/gnopreview: wantFile is declared at crawl.go:227 and called once, from inScope at crawl.go:209; TestWantFile (crawl_test.go:196-228) calls c.inScope on four URLs and c.chargeFile in the budget loop.

dropped.settled_by: Applied the rewrite (fixture built by urlToFile, want updated to the real digest) and widened slug()'s digest to sha256[:6]: the rewrite turns TestMapURL red — `mapURL("/r/x/y$source&file=a.gno") = "../../../r/x/y/_t/file-a.gno-source-adc2ecdcb13b/"` — on a change with nothing to do with mapURL, while TestURLToFile already caught that drift at head (`--- FAIL: TestURLToFile ... want "r/gnoland/home/_t/file-home.gno-source-2ca84ba4/index.html"`). The synthetic fixture is the right call: it keeps mapURL's test independent of slug().
